topics.title: Complete the Words
topics.scope: A short academic paragraph (60-95 words): the first sentence is whole, then exactly 10 words have their second half missing; the test taker types the missing letters. Tests vocabulary, word forms, grammar and meaning from context.

topics.title: Read in Daily Life: short texts
topics.scope: Short everyday texts (25-80 words): notices, signs, text messages, menus, social media posts, short emails, timetables. 2 questions each: purpose, detail, meaning of a phrase, what the reader should do.

topics.title: Read in Daily Life: longer texts
topics.scope: Longer everyday texts (90-160 words): emails, campus announcements, flyers, product instructions, schedules, web pages, message threads. 3 questions each: purpose, detail, inference, vocabulary, next action.

topics.title: Read an Academic Passage
topics.scope: Academic passages of 170-230 words (life and earth science, history, art, psychology, business, technology) with 5 questions: main idea, detail, inference, vocabulary in context, reference, purpose of a sentence, organization, negative fact.

topics.title: Listen and Choose a Response
topics.scope: One speaker says a short line (a question, request, complaint or remark, 4-20 words); choose the most natural reply from four written responses. Tests pragmatic meaning, idioms and indirect answers.

topics.title: Listen to a Conversation
topics.scope: Short conversations between two speakers (80-150 words, 6-10 turns) in campus or everyday settings, 2 questions each: main topic, detail, speaker's purpose or attitude, what happens next.

topics.title: Listen to an Announcement
topics.scope: Announcements or voicemails by one speaker (70-130 words): class changes, campus events, facility rules, field trips, deadlines. 2 questions each: purpose, detail, what listeners must do.

topics.title: Listen to an Academic Talk
topics.scope: Short lectures or academic talks by one speaker (160-250 words), science, social science, humanities, business. 4 questions each: main idea, detail, purpose of an example, speaker's attitude, organization, inference.

topics.title: Build a Sentence
topics.scope: A line from one person in a short exchange; the reply is built by putting 4-7 word chunks in the right order (sometimes with one extra chunk that does not belong). Tests word order: questions, embedded questions, tenses, relative clauses, adverb placement.

topics.title: Write an Email
topics.scope: A practical situation (about 60-100 words) and three things the email must do; write an email of about 100-150 words in 7 minutes with the right tone.

topics.title: Write for an Academic Discussion
topics.scope: A professor's question on a class discussion board and two students' posts; write a contribution of at least 100 words in 10 minutes that states and supports an opinion.

topics.title: Listen and Repeat
topics.scope: A scenario (e.g. training as a museum guide) and 7 sentences to repeat exactly, getting longer and more complex (4 to about 20 words).

topics.title: Take an Interview
topics.scope: A scenario (e.g. a research study about city life) and 4 interview questions, from personal and familiar to opinion and prediction; 45 seconds to answer each, no preparation time.
